newsitem.title: UK: Copper rises away from $2,000, awaits stock data.
newsitem.headline: Copper rises away from $2,000, awaits stock data.

text.p: London Metal Exchange (LME) copper prices extended an earlier recovery back above the $2,000 a tonne level during Monday evening business, preparing for Tuesday's warehouse stock data, traders said.
Latest talk on copper inventories is for a fall of some 5,000 tonnes. Currently, stocks stand at six-year lows of 113,400 tonnes.

However, the market is not really responding to the recent run of headline stock declines, with some suspicion over whether metal is being consumed or being moved around from area to area for other purposes.
On the charts resistance is pegged at $2,040, and support is seen at $1,985.
"As long as we do not get a nasty shock on tomorrow's stock figures, the market seems to be content to straddle $2,000 at present," one trader said.
At 1900 gmt copper was indicated at $2,015/18, against Friday's $2,007 close.
Aluminium was quoted at $1,451/54, compared with a pre-weekend level of $1,450.
